abstracts.abstract: Data quality management in contemporary information systems remains predominantly anchored in static, snapshot-based evaluation paradigms that fail to capture the inherently dynamic nature of data artifacts in operational contexts. This paper introduces the Contextual Data Quality Dynamics (CDQD) framework, a novel theoretical paradigm reconceptualizing data quality as an emergent, relationship-dependent property rather than an intrinsic attribute. Drawing upon complexity theory and actor-network perspectives, the CDQD framework posits that data quality manifests through continuous negotiation among data objects, processing workflows, and contextual stakeholders within information systems ecosystems. The methodology comprises three interconnected theoretical constructs: (1) a formal specification language for modeling quality emergence patterns, (2) a multi-dimensional interaction model capturing relational quality dependencies, and (3) a dynamic assessment mechanism accounting for temporal and contextual variations. The framework's explanatory power is validated through a multi-case analysis of data quality phenomena in enterprise database systems, demonstrating its capacity to generate insights unattainable through conventional approaches. By shifting the analytical focus from isolated quality attributes to emergent quality dynamics, this paradigmatic contribution establishes a new theoretical foundation for understanding how information quality arises, evolves, and can be systematically managed in complex organizational settings.

Knowledge management in distributed enterprise systems confronts fundamental challenges in achieving semantic interoperability across heterogeneous information repositories. Existing ontological alignment approaches operate under simplifying assumptions of stable conceptual structures, rendering them inadequate for dynamic organizational environments where domain ontologies continuously evolve. This paper presents the Adaptive Ontology Dynamics (AOD) framework, a substantially enhanced theoretical model that extends conventional ontology matching techniques to accommodate semantic drift and conceptual evolution. The AOD framework introduces three novel theoretical mechanisms: (1) a temporal semantics model capturing concept transformations over time, (2) a context-sensitive alignment function incorporating situational factors into matching decisions, and (3) a semantic coherence preservation principle ensuring logical consistency during alignment processes. The methodology employs probabilistic reasoning over concept evolution histories, enabling predictive alignment that anticipates future semantic divergence. Analytical validation through formal proofs demonstrates that the AOD framework achieves alignment precision exceeding 94% in simulated environments with varying degrees of semantic dynamism, representing a substantial improvement over state-of-the-art approaches that typically achieve 76-82% precision under similar conditions. The framework's theoretical contributions include a comprehensive taxonomy of ontology evolution patterns and a unified semantic distance metric incorporating temporal dimensions. This work provides information systems researchers and practitioners with a principled foundation for addressing the persistent challenge of maintaining semantic coherence in knowledge management systems operating in volatile domains.

The exponential growth of streaming data from IoT devices and digital platforms has exposed fundamental limitations in conventional data stream processing architectures, which typically employ rigid, centrally-coordinated paradigms incapable of adapting to heterogeneous source characteristics and varying quality requirements. This paper introduces StreamForge, a novel distributed computing architecture that embodies a paradigm shift from centralized to federated stream processing. The architecture introduces three foundational design principles: (1) hierarchical edge-cloud coordination enabling intelligent workload distribution, (2) adaptive quality-aware data fusion mechanisms dynamically adjusting processing fidelity based on downstream consumption requirements, and (3) self-organizing stream semantics allowing processing operators to collectively negotiate data transformation pipelines. The system design incorporates a lightweight metadata registry and a decentralized orchestration engine that collectively enable resilient, context-aware stream processing without requiring global synchronization. Implementation and evaluation across diverse deployment scenarios demonstrate that StreamForge reduces end-to-end processing latency by 62% compared to Apache Flink-based baselines while maintaining 99.2% result accuracy for analytical workloads. The architecture exhibits linear scalability across 10,000+ processing nodes and graceful degradation under adversarial network conditions. By fundamentally reimagining the relationship between data streams and processing infrastructure, StreamForge establishes a new design paradigm for building intelligent, context-adaptive streaming systems capable of operating effectively across the continuum from edge devices to cloud data centers.

Enterprise data warehouse systems increasingly struggle to balance query performance optimization against the overhead of index maintenance and storage consumption, particularly as data volumes grow and query patterns become more diverse. Traditional approaches employing static indexing strategies fail to adapt to workload evolution, resulting in suboptimal resource utilization and degraded system responsiveness. This paper presents AdaptiveIndex++, an enhanced data warehouse indexing framework that significantly improves upon existing adaptive indexing techniques through three key innovations: (1) a machine learning-driven workload prediction module that anticipates query patterns and preemptively prepares appropriate index structures, (2) a multi-objective optimization engine balancing query performance, index maintenance overhead, and storage utilization based on configurable business priorities, and (3) an incremental index refinement mechanism enabling continuous optimization without system downtime. The system design integrates seamlessly with existing data warehouse platforms through a transparent indexing layer abstraction. Comprehensive evaluation using the TPC-DS benchmark suite and real-world enterprise workloads demonstrates that AdaptiveIndex++ achieves 47% improvement in average query response time and 58% reduction in storage footprint compared to conventional index management approaches, while maintaining query result accuracy above 99.7%. The framework exhibits robust adaptation across diverse workload characteristics and scales effectively to multi-terabyte datasets. This work provides organizations with a practical, significantly improved solution for optimizing data warehouse performance through intelligent, automated index management.
